/ Readiness checklist

DFARS 252.225-7052 readiness checklist

For small and midsize defense suppliers of motors, actuators and other parts that may contain NdFeB or SmCo magnets, tungsten or tantalum. Clause dated May 2024; upstream stages (mining, refining, separation) in scope from 1 January 2027. Checked 15 October 2026.

Download PDF

1. Scope

  • We know which of our contracts and purchase orders include DFARS 252.225-7052, directly or by flow-down.
  • We have a list of part numbers that may contain NdFeB or SmCo magnets, tungsten, or tantalum.
  • For each of those parts, we know the direct supplier and, where possible, the magnet or metal maker behind it.
  • Our contracts team has confirmed whether any exception may apply. (We have not assumed one.)

2. Records by stage

For each in-scope part, can you point to a dated document that names the facility and country for each stage?

  • Mining of the ore or feedstock (including recycled feed)
  • Separation and refining
  • Metal and alloy making (melting)
  • Final production of the magnet or metal part

A declaration that covers only the magnet maker or finished part usually leaves the earlier stages open.

3. Quality of the documents

  • Each document says which stage it covers, not just "origin".
  • Each document is dated and still applies to the lots we ship.
  • We know who issued each document and how to reach them.
  • Where a supplier could not answer, we have recorded that and know who upstream can.

4. Readiness for customer questions

  • We can answer a prime's or higher-tier customer's origin request for our top parts within a week.
  • We know which parts have open questions, and what we have asked suppliers.
  • We do not send drawings, controlled technical data or export-controlled information in these requests.
  • Someone owns this internally (quality, purchasing or contracts) and reviews it when suppliers change.
Several unchecked boxes is normal today, especially in section 2. A readiness call takes about 30 minutes and helps you decide which parts to start with.

Lodeline provides supply-chain documentation and analysis, not legal advice or government certification. Applicability, exceptions, and acceptance depend on the contract and the responsible reviewer.
